title: A segment cut short because its input ended early is never stored, however the worker's upload check and ffmpeg's exit are ordered
description: Read from two merge-queue runs on 2026-11-20 (JS-155's record, not reproduced): a job whose source read was cut for good failed, yet its request was answered with a segment and no error. As read, the worker's periodic upload check can store the cut-short segment ffmpeg flushes on the way out before the worker sees ffmpeg exit, and only the exit path applies invariant 40. A viewer would get a freeze or jump of up to about 4 s at that place, as would every viewer of that spec until its segments are swept, and no failure is reported. DOMAINS.md invariant 40; PRODUCT.md: seeking and resuming just work; every failure is reported with its reason. D-043.
acceptanceCriteria: Before any fix, on main as it stands after JS-168 and JS-173, under CI's shape (ffmpeg 6.1, two CPUs no other run is using, a fresh database each run), each cut-read subtest of internal/transcode/recovery_integration_test.go is run 20 times: the three of TestAFailureThatIsNotTheFilesIsMadeAgainForTheRequestThatWaited (a re-encode, a copy, a burn-in) and the one of TestACauseThatPersistsStartsAtMostThreeFreshJobsAndThenFails. The runs and failures of each are recorded in docs/testing.md with each failure's message.

For the waiting-request case, the record says what the 24 bytes are (which MP4 boxes, and whether they hold any frame), which path stored or answered them (the worker's periodic upload check, its exit path, or something else), and whether the cause is this task's (a cut-short segment stored before the exit is seen) or another.

A check with real ffmpeg, under CI's shape, forces this order: ffmpeg has put its cut-short last segment in place and is held before it exits, and the worker's upload check then runs. The check asserts that the order really happened (an upload check ran while the cut segment was in place and ffmpeg was still alive), so a hold that silently misses cannot pass. On today's code it fails because that segment is stored. If it cannot be made to fail, nothing is built: the sighting's verdict returns to cause unknown and the product owner is told.

After the fix, in that order and in the opposite one (the exit seen before the next upload check), no segment shorter than its place is stored for the spec, and none is served to the waiting request or to a later request from another viewer through another stream replica. This holds for each of 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 combinations: the cut at segment 0 and at a segment at least 2 into the film; a re-encode and a copied stream; a source read that fails for good and a file that ends early; a cut that leaves the place with no frame and one that leaves about half of it.

In those same runs, every whole segment made before the cut (at least two in the later-segment case) is stored exactly once and served with its full length, and the place where the cut fell and every place after it have no stored object when the job ends.

The film's true last segment is still stored and served in both orders, for a re-encode and a copy: the playlist's last segment, within 1.5 s of the playlist's length for it. A last segment more than 1.5 s short is still refused, as invariant 40 says.

With ffmpeg held just after it has put a whole segment in place (not at its exit), that segment is stored and served while ffmpeg is held. A fix that keeps every segment back until the next one is made or ffmpeg exits fails this.

A file that ends early: the waiting request gets the failure "the input ended early". Exactly one job runs, with no fresh job within failureMemory, and PlaybackInfo (Jobs.Unavailable) refuses the spec with the memory of that failure.

A source read that fails for good: the waiting request gets the failure that names the source store, not "the input ended early", after at most three fresh jobs (at most four jobs in all), and every one of those jobs ends failed.

Each failed job above is logged with its reason and counted once in jellyscale_transcode_jobs_ended_total{result="failed"}. A job that failed in the forced order is counted as failed, never done or interrupted.

Recorded with ids and counts only (no title or path), stating the window of logs read: how many dogfood jobs failed on an early input end or a source read, and how many of those stored a segment at the place where they stopped, or that the logs cannot tell. If any stored one, the product owner gets a brief on the segments already stored before any purge is built.

Start of play and seek on a healthy film are measured before and after the fix: the time to first segment for a re-encode and a copy, at segment 0 and at a seek, at least 10 runs each on the same pinned shape. The figures are logged and recorded as a record, not a bar (docs/testing.md, Mechanisms not speeds). If the after median is above the before median by more than the spread of the before runs, that goes to the lead as a finding.

No product code changes to fit a check, and nothing is retried or skipped. These stay as they are: the 100 ms upload poll, maxRestarts (3), failureMemory, recoveryWait, the stall limit, the 1.5 s last-segment bound, and every existing check's waits.

DOMAINS.md invariant 40 says the guarantee holds on every path that stores a segment: while ffmpeg runs and at its exit, for a re-encode and for a copy (and so for the encodes that share the copy's path). docs/testing.md's JS-155 row for this sighting carries its new verdict and runs, and docs/status.md is updated if it speaks of it.

No other viewer-visible change: a healthy film played to its end as a re-encode and as a copy stores every segment of its playlist exactly once and no job fails. The existing checks of internal/transcode and internal/api pass unamended.

If the waiting-request case has another cause, nothing is built for it here. It returns to the product owner as a brief with what a viewer would see (a broken segment, a stated failure, or a retry), and JS-159 finishes without it.

After the fix, the persisting-cause subtest passes 20 of 20 under CI's shape: the failure names the source store after at most three fresh jobs, with no segment stored for its place. If the waiting-request case's cause is this task's, its three cut-read subtests also pass 20 of 20, each answered with a whole segment (over 1000 bytes, frames for its full place) made by a fresh job. No check is amended, retried, skipped or given a longer wait.
source: JS-155 record (merge-queue runs of #225 and #230); D-042; D-043
notes: core: true. Check runs must not run while JS-154 is measuring on the same machine. Segments already stored short stay until the sweep unless the dogfood count shows any. Moved from 25 to 16 and amended by D-057; builds beside JS-161. Core: true; it and JS-158 may run together, but neither runs its checks on a machine where JS-174 is measuring. Done 2026-11-23 (#257). Criterion 6 (the dogfood count) closed as not taken by D-061: the logs cover only the pod's life and no ended job is kept.
